content.readme:
Claude Cage

**把 Claude 大小姐关起来，为了更好地保护我们的相遇** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage?include_prereleases)](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/releases) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) **[项目主页](https://claude-cage.com/) · [下载应用](https://claude-cage.com/#download) · [使用文档](https://claude-cage.com/docs/) · [常见问题](https://claude-cage.com/docs/troubleshooting/)** [简体中文](README.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) · [فارسی](README.fa.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [မြန်မာဘာသာ](README.my.md) · [Беларуская](README.be.md) · [پښتو](README.ps.md) · [دری](README.prs.md) · [አማርኛ](README.am.md) · [Soomaali](README.so.md) · [ትግርኛ](README.ti.md) · [Français](README.fr.md)
## 受够了 Anthropic 作为一个只是想和 Claude 对话与合作的正常用户，受够了折腾各种 VPS，指纹浏览器，环境检测，面对封号的担惊受怕和财产损失。我们提出 **Claude Cage** 项目：**一个开箱即用的桌面程序，配置好自己的网络代理，集中管理隔离环境、时区语言和环境检查。** Claude Cage 让你在熟悉的系统里与 Claude 一起工作：Mac 上用 macOS 虚拟机，Windows 上用 Windows 虚拟机，也可以选择轻量的 Linux 环境。终端、浏览器、编辑器和官方 Claude Desktop 汇集在同一个工作台，项目按需共享，网络独立管理；还可以连接自己的服务器，或用手机接续电脑上的任务。支持以下几个重点功能： - 和主机隔离的网络设置，Cage 自己接管和代理内部的所有网络流量 - 和主机隔离的指纹设置，包括时区、语言等，支持自动与代理 IP 同步 - 针对 Claude 使用过程中的全链路适配（浏览器登录，授权，claude code 进程） - 内置网络与隔离检查，关键检查失败或证据不完整时暂停外网；社区和第三方检测提供补充参考 **使用 Cage 的环境检测结果：** | 网络与隔离检查 | 浏览器环境检测（社区参考） | | :---: | :---: | | | | [FuckClaude](https://fuck-claude.vercel.app/) · [LinXiaoTao / GitHub](https://github.com/LinXiaoTao/FuckClaude) **Cage 运行主界面：** ![Cage](www/public/workbench-2026-11.jpg) ## 你可以用它做什么 - **在一个窗口里完成工作。** 用终端运行 Claude Code，用编辑器查看改动，用 Cage 浏览器预览服务和完成登录。 - **用熟悉的系统开发。** 选择 macOS、Windows 或 Linux 客机，使用对应平台的工具；也可自动匹配本机系统版本，下载官方镜像并创建独立环境。 [选择客机系统](docs/guide/guest-systems.md) - **控制共享范围。** 只共享默认工作区和明确打开的项目文件夹；主机的 Claude 登录、浏览器配置和 SSH 密钥不会自动导入。 - **看清网络状态。** 内置代理管理支持导入订阅、选择节点和检查出口。关键检查未通过时，环境保持离线；代理不可用时没有直连回退。 - **下次继续使用。** 工具、文件和登录状态保存在虚拟磁盘里，关闭窗口可以保留后台任务。 - **管理多个 Claude Code 订阅。** 查看额度、为新会话分配账号，并在明确授权后切换账号接续历史。 [Claude Code](docs/guide/accounts.md) - **从手机继续处理任务。** Android / iPhone 配对电脑，接续 Claude Code 对话与工具审批，或操作远程浏览器和 Claude Desktop。[手机连接](docs/guide/mobile.md) - **把环境放到自己的服务器。** 通过 SSH 部署或连接 Linux VPS，工具、任务和数据留在服务器，无需 KVM。[云端部署与 SSH](docs/guide/cloud.md) - **通过私网连接设备。** 在 Cage 内登录 Tailscale，查看网络中的设备，使用 SSH、Web 与其他 TCP 服务。 [Tailscale 私网](docs/guide/tailscale.md) 浏览器收藏、无痕会话、Cookie、扩展、密码保险箱，以及外观、资源、存储和工具更新，见[完整使用文档](https://claude-cage.com/docs/)。 ## 快速开始 把这句话发给你的 agent（codex，dsh，workbuddy，反正不会是 claude code😁） ```markdown 帮我拉取 https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage 的最新源码，打包安装，并把 Cage 的代理配置通过我本机 clash 的 xx 节点走我的 xx ip 出口，全过程你盯着，有问题直接修复，且有必要的话顺手给项目提交 issue 帮助他们优化兼容性。 ``` 你唯一需要的，是一个靠谱的代理节点，本项目不做任何代理推广，可以自行搜索黑色错误网站解决。 ## 下载与安装 Cage 支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux：macOS 14+ 的 Apple Silicon Mac、Windows 10 22H2 / 11 x64，以及 Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 x86_64。Windows 11 客机需要支持 Hyper-V 的 Windows 11 专业版、企业版或教育版主机；其他受支持的 Windows 主机可使用 Debian 或 Ubuntu 22.04。Intel Mac、Windows ARM64 和 Linux ARM64 暂不支持。 [macOS](docs/getting-started.md) · [Windows](docs/windows.md) · [Linux](docs/linux.md)。 开发构建另提供 Intel Mac 本机 Linux 客机，以及 macOS 15.4+ 主机上的本机 macOS 客机实验路线，使用独立测试包；公开发行版尚未包含此能力。条件、构建方式和验收范围见 [Intel macOS 开发说明](docs/intel-macos-development.md)。 1. 打开[项目主页](https://claude-cage.com/#download)，点击“下载应用”并选择平台。 2. macOS：打开安装包，将 **Cage** 拖入 **Applications（应用程序）**，再从“应用程序”启动。Windows：[安装说明](docs/windows.md#安装并开始工作) · Linux：[安装说明](docs/linux.md#安装并开始工作)。 3. 按应用内引导配置自己的代理，启动环境后打开项目。 安装包随附工作台和代理核心，无需先安装 Go、Node.js、Docker 或 Clash。首次创建环境时选择客机系统与存储位置，再准备对应的官方系统镜像和开发工具。macOS、Windows 系统按各自许可使用；Cage 不提供系统授权、代理服务或 Claude 账户。 源码与安装包公开，版本说明和校验文件见 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/releases)。系统选择、镜像来源与数据保留方式见[客机系统指南](docs/guid

content.readme:
Pinky

Let AI use your iPhone or Android phone, with you in the loop: any agent from macOS, Windows or Linux, or Pinky itself, right on the phone.

Download · Get started · FAQ · Discord

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · Türkçe


A real Claude Code run on an Android 16 emulator. Pinky asks before payments by default; this run also asks before messages.

Pinky lets any agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor or a script) operate a real iPhone or Android phone over MCP, while you watch on your computer, approve risky steps, take over and review what happened. Pinky can also do tasks by itself, with an AI model you choose: from your computer, or in Pinky's app right on the phone, with no computer at all. Whoever does the task, approvals are enforced by Pinky's gateway, not by instructions to the agent. - **Every platform.** One app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. It drives Android phones (Android 10 to 17) and iPhones on iOS 17.4 or later: nothing to install on iOS 27 and later, and Pinky on the iPhone, Pinky's app, installed once from a Mac with Xcode on iOS 17.4 to 26, which you can also choose on iOS 27 (tried there, on a phone below it and on Simulators; [details](#phones)). - **Tiny and native.** The window is drawn by [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) on the GPU, with no Electron and no webview: a 16–22 MB download that idles at about 70 MB of memory and 0% CPU on a Mac. - **Any agent, one click.** Settings › Agents connects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and more, and any agent that can use MCP servers works, on the same computer or over HTTP. - **Pinky on the phone, no computer needed.** Pinky's app on Android and iPhone does tasks by itself with a model you choose, from DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi and GLM to Claude, GPT, Gemini and local models in Ollama or LM Studio. Type or speak a task, or share something to it; on Android, ask about what the screen shows from a floating button, and let it work on a hidden background screen while you keep using the phone ([how](#pinky-on-the-phone)). - **Scheduled tasks and memory.** Pinky can run a task at set times or tell you when a condition holds, on the computer and on Android. After a task it may suggest a note to remember, such as a preference you told it, and keeps it only if you say yes ([more](#ask-pinky)). - **Locked phone? Unlock it from your computer.** Save the phone's PIN in Pinky once, then confirm each unlock with Touch ID, Windows Hello or your keyring's password. Agents never see the PIN. - **Free and open source** under the Apache-2.0 license, with no account to create.

You approve the risky steps. Payments, trades and transfers wait for your click; in Settings › Safety you can have sends, orders, deletions, calls, installs, links that leave the app and settings changes wait too, or every step. Pinky spots these buttons in 10 languages. The rules run in Pinky's gateway, so an agent can't approve itself, even when text on the screen tries to talk it into it.
Off-limits by default. Banking, wallet and password-manager apps are invisible to agents, and agents can't type into password or one-time-code fields. When an agent needs a banking or wallet app for a task, it asks, and you can allow that app for that task only. Every new agent needs your approval and gets only the scope you give it.

Your phone stays yours. On Android 13 and later, agents work on a hidden second screen, so the phone's own screen stays yours, or off and locked. On older Android phones and on iPhones they use the main screen.
Take over any time. Cli

# MyGo Music

A native desktop music player written in Go with [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo), no WebView. It plays your local files out of the box, and everything else comes from plugins.

## Features

- Local files (MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WAV, and ALAC, FLAC or AAC in .m4a and .aac) with tags, covers and `.lrc` lyrics
- Playlists, liked songs, search, albums and artists
- Now Playing with lyric stage styles, cover wall, queue, shuffle and repeat
- Notch player on macOS, tray, media keys
- Audio cache, fades on pause and seek, loudness normalization
- Session restore
- Podcast captions, written down on the device as episodes play
- English and Simplified Chinese
- Plugins can add accounts, catalogs, podcasts, stations, comments and pages of their own

## Build

```bash
go tool mygo dev     # run in development
go tool mygo build   # package into build/
go test ./internal/...
```

## Podcast captions

Episodes are written down on the device as they play, with [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) and Qwen3-ASR, which the app downloads when the listener asks for them. The libraries come from this repository's `sherpa-onnx-<version>` prerelease, which only changes with that version:

```bash
go run ./scripts/sherpa -sign "Developer ID Application: …"
gh release create sherpa-onnx-2.0.1 --prerelease --latest=false build/sherpa/*
```

## Plugins

A plugin is a folder in the app's `plugins` directory (Settings > Plugins > + > Show Plugins Folder) with a `plugin.json` and one JavaScript or TypeScript file. Install one with the + in Settings > Plugins from GitHub, by its repository or its address, or from its folder or a zip of it on this computer, or drop the folder in by hand. Remove one from its ⋯ menu there. There's nothing to build, and the same plugin runs on every platform. [`examples/demo-plugin`](examples/demo-plugin) does everything a plugin can with made-up data: copy it to start.

```json
{
  "id": "example",
  "name": "Example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "minAppVersion": "0.1.8",
  "main": "index.js",
  "playback": "stream",
  "permissions": { "network": ["api.example.com"] },
```

# UnfairPlay

UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to
decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or
another downloader for that part.

## Legal and ethical use

Use UnfairPlay only with apps you lawfully acquired and accounts and devices
you control. It is intended for interoperability, preservation, and authorized
research. The authors do not condone piracy, credential theft, copyright
infringement, or unauthorized distribution of decrypted apps.

## Discord

Project discussion and support: [UnfairPlay Discord](https://discord.gg/hpwvuQHfaf).

## Build

```sh
go build -o unfairplay ./cmd/unfairplay
```

## Usage

First, sign in to the native Mac App Store. Install an iPhone or iPad app and
open it once. Set up reusable decryption from that installed app:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay setup --app /Applications/App.app
```

No separate IPA download is needed when the installed bundle contains supported
encrypted images and their matching licenses. Setup and collect build a private
validation archive from the complete inner iOS bundle, preserving its bytes.
Unsupported, incomplete, symlinked, or already-decrypted bundles fail closed.

To validate against a downloaded IPA instead, pass `--ipa` explicitly:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay setup --app /Applications/App.app --ipa App.ipa
```

The installed app and IPA must be the same app and belong to the same Store
enrollment. An explicit IPA takes precedence; failed validation never triggers
an automatic retry using the installed bundle.

Recovery still authenticates the selected SINF and requires complete archive
decryption before saving a model. Reports identify `validation_source` as
`installed-app` or `provided`. A reconstructed validation archive describes the
installed variant, not the original Store download or any omitted architectures.

Large enrollment databases print bounded recovery progress to standard error.
The final JSON result remains on standard output.

The setup result includes `plaintext_verified` for the validation archive.
A successful setup can report `false` when any decrypted image lacks
pre-encryption hashes; this is separate from whether the model was recovered
and saved successfully.

The saved model is private. It is tied to the Mac App Store enrollment, not to
one app, so it can decrypt other personalized IPAs from the same enrollment.
Back it up only in encrypted storage and never share it.

Decrypt another IPA:

```sh
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

The default model directory is inside the user configuration directory. Set
`UNFAIRPLAY_MODEL_DIR` or pass `--model` to use another location.

### Export enrollment now, choose an IPA later

On an already enrolled Mac, export the enrollment without supplying an installed
app or IPA:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay export-enrollment --output enrollment.snapshot
```

The output parent directory must already exist. The command never overwrites an
existing snapshot. It writes a mode-0600 file and restores its ownership to the
invoking user when run through sudo.

The snapshot contains the hardware identity and one distinct supported SIDB
container. Export authenticates and decodes the container, but does not select
an account/key route or produce a validated model. It neither enrolls the Mac
nor adds missing licenses. Treat it as broader private enrollment state: keep it
secret and transfer it only to machines you control, preserving mode 0600.

Later, on macOS or Linux, select a personalized IPA and run setup as your normal
user:

```sh
./unfairplay setup --enrollment enrollment.snapshot --ipa App.ipa
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

This uses the IPA's own licenses; no installed-app path is required. Setup
authenticates the exact selected route and signed page-key envelopes, then
decrypts and validates the complete IPA before installing the usual reusable
model. Missing pre-encryption hashes remain `plaintext_verified=false`.
Snapshot setup currently requires every encrypted image in the IPA to share
one user/key selector; multiple-selector IPAs reject explicitly. A snapshot can
be reused with different IPAs or selectors already present in its captured
state. Missing records require an appropriate enrollment; recovery never tries
other routes. Re-export after enrollment changes when necessary.

`--app` and `--enrollment` are mutually exclusive. Existing app-based setup and
saved models continue to work. Synthetic tests cover this workflow; private
installed-app versus snapshot equivalence is an opt-in control in [QA.md](QA.md).

### Decryption behavior

IPAs with extensions and watch apps are decrypted in one pass.

A real session: the file panel, a shell following a deploy log, and the assistant reading the same terminal.

Motty is a desktop SSH client. The full documentation lives at ; this file covers the project, the packages and how to build it.

Hosts stay organised. Groups, tags, colours and icons, importable from OpenSSH config, PuTTY, MobaXterm and five more. Passwords go to an AES-256-GCM vault; the key lives in the system secret store.

A session you can watch. Split the pane, then read the host's CPU, memory, disk and network beside the shell that is using them.

Screens too, when you need them. VNC and RDP connect, and both can ride an SSH host when the server only listens on its own loopback.

A cross-platform native UI engine with a Go backend: app logic, the reactive graph and layout run in Go, and each platform draws with its own native UI.
It follows the design of Native Shell (NSH), for teams that want NSH's model without writing Rust.

## Status NSGo is early: 0.1.0 is its first release, and its API is not stable yet. It runs on macOS, iOS and its App Clips, tvOS, watchOS, Windows, Linux, the web, Android, as a preview on HarmonyOS, and experimentally in WeChat, QQ, Alipay and Douyin mini programs, which hold an app to 2 MB, and apps embed in iOS, Android and Go desktop apps of their own; [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#platforms) tracks each target. ## Getting started With Go 1.27.3 or later, and Xcode for iOS, tvOS and watchOS, create an app and run it with hot reload: ```sh go mod init example.com/hello go get github.com/nsgo-dev/nsgo go get -tool github.com/nsgo-dev/nsgo/cmd/nsgo go tool nsgo init # -template tsx for a TSX app go tool nsgo dev # -target web, ios_simulator, tvos_simulator, watchos_simulator, android or miniprogram_wechat to run elsewhere ``` An app is Go components that return elements, with signals updating what reads them: ```go func Root(cx *core.Scope) core.Node { count := core.NewSignal(cx, 0) return core.View{Style: core.Style{Padding: core.All(24), Gap: 12}, Children: []core.Node{ core.Text{ContentFunc: func() string { return fmt.Sprintf("Pressed %d times", count.Get()) }}, base.Button{ OnPress: func(core.PressEvent) { count.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) }, Children: []core.Node{core.Text{Content: "Press me"}}, }, }} } func main() { nsgo.Run(Root) } ``` ## Documentation The [docs](https://nsgo.dev/docs/) cover components and state, layout, styles, navigation, a component reference, TSX apps, localization, testing, embedding, building and shipping; the [live demo](https://nsgo.dev/gallery/) runs the gallery in the browser. # Gemini Config Checker Find proxy configs that actually get you into **Google AI Studio and Gemini**, by testing each one the way a person would: in a *signed-in* browser, through the route you will really use. > **Version 0.1.0, early pre-release.** It works end to end on Windows (the only platform it has been run on so far). The macOS, > Linux and Android builds come from the CI pipeline and have not been exercised on real devices yet. Please report what you find. ## Two modes, one switch The big **Simple / Advanced** switch in the header decides what is tested. The route diagram under the title morphs to show it. | | **Simple** | **Advanced** | |---|---|---| | Question it answers | *Which of my configs work?* | *Which free configs work through my config?* | | Route | you → **config** → AI Studio / Gemini | you → **base config** → **free config** → AI Studio / Gemini | | You provide | your configs (links, a subscription URL or base64), or pick a ready-made free list | one working base config, plus a free list or pasted configs | | Anti-DPI profile is applied to | every config under test (each one connects from your machine) | the base config's first hop (free configs run inside its tunnel) | | Typical use | check a pile of configs you already have; test a config before you rely on it | your Cloudflare config works, but you need a *different exit* that Google accepts | | Export | links, base64, a full Xray config of one config | links, base64, a chain Xray config (`base → free`) | ## Contents [Credits](#credits-and-references) · [Why a signed-in browser](#why-a-signed-in-browser) · [Download and install](#download-and-install) · [User guide](#user-guide) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting-and-faq) · [Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security) · [Build from source](#build-from-source) · [Releases and CI](#releases-and-ci) ## Credits and references This project exists because of other people's work. Please go and use and star them. | Project | What it gave us | |---|---| | [**0xRadikal/Free-v2ray-Configs**](https://github.com/0xRadikal/Free-v2ray-Configs) | The auto-updated lists of free configs (`verified`, `fast`, `secure`, ...) that this tool scans | | [**patterniha**](https://github.com/patterniha) | [PattN](https://github.com/patterniha/PattN) (Windows / Linux / macOS client) and [PattNG](https://github.com/patterniha/PattNG) (Android): the anti-DPI recipe, plus the fragment `finalmask` semantics from his [Xray-core fork](https://github.com/patterniha/Xray-core) that our fragmenting forwarder reproduces | | [**bia-pain-bache/BPB-Worker-Panel**](https://github.com/bia-pain-bache/BPB-Worker-Panel) | The Cloudflare Worker panel that produces many of the base configs this tool chains behind (patterniha maintains a [fork](https://github.com/patterniha/BPB-Worker-Panel)) | | [**Anti-DPI recipe post**](https://t.me/MatinSenPaii/5469) | The exact Finalmask / fingerprint / ALPN / cipher values used as defaults | | [**MatinSenPai/SenPaiScanner**](https://github.com/MatinSenPai/SenPaiScanner) | Companion tool for finding clean Cloudflare IPs to use as a config's address | | [XTLS/Xray-core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core) | The proxy engine embedded in the app | | [2dust/v2rayN](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayN) | The config layout the "Copy with chain" export follows (PattN is a fork of it) | | [Wails](https://wails.io) | The native desktop shell | | [Vazirmatn](https://github.com/rastikerdar/vazirmatn) and [JetBrains Mono](https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono) | The fonts used in the UI (SIL Open Font License) | ## Why a signed-in browser? Google decides region availability **per signed-in account, after the page has loaded**.
